To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) integrity constraints are not sufficient to guarantee the integrity of a relational database; (ii) the integrity objectives can be achieved with integrity principles, which are a set of integrity constraints, integrity rules, and integrity actions; (iii) a DBMS must provide integrity mechanisms that support the integrity objectives; and (iv) the integrity mechanisms are: integrity constraint specification, integrity constraint checking, integrity constraint enforcement, integrity rule checking and enforcement, and integrity action checking and enforcement.

integrity constraints can be specified in the relational algebra in terms of the relational algebra operations and that these constraints can be enforced by a combination of the relational algebra operators, integrity checking and integrity enforcing triggers, and integrity enforcing views.

(1) the mechanisms of relational DBMSs can be extended to provide integrity mechanisms; (2) these mechanisms can be provided in a way that does not require the user to be aware of the underlying database structure; and (3) these mechanisms can also be provided in a manner that allows the user to be fully aware of the database structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integrity principles and mechanisms that are necessary for a general-purpose database management system to provide a high level of data integrity.

the following questions: What are the requirements for integrity in information systems? What are the mechanisms for integrity in DBMSs? What is the role of security in integrity? How do the mechanisms for integrity and security interact?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a general-purpose DBMS must provide the following mechanisms to facilitate the integrity requirements of an information system: 1. A mechanism to define and enforce constraints. 2. A mechanism to specify the integrity objectives of the system. 3. A mechanism to ensure that integrity objectives are met.

a DBMS must provide mechanisms to: - ensure that all updates to the data in the database are authorized and consistent with the integrity rules of the database. - ensure that all queries to the data are authorized. - ensure that data are not disclosed to users who are unauthorized to access them. - ensure that users are not able to access the database in ways not intended by the DBMS designer.
the integrity objectives of an information system can be achieved by using the mechanisms of the DBMS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to provide an integrated and comprehensive framework for integrity in database systems.
integrity is a fundamental and important issue for database management systems.
integrity principles can be incorporated into a general-purpose relational DBMS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integrity objectives of an organization can be met by the use of the relational model of data and by the application of integrity mechanisms that can be easily incorporated in a relational DBMS.
the mechanisms we propose are not specific to the relational DBMS paradigm, but can be extended to object-oriented DBMSs.
the integrity objectives of an information system can be achieved in a multiuser DBMS by a combination of integrity constraints and access control.
